previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening bilateral lower extremity pain, erythema, and malodorous discharge concerning for infection. Wound culture confirmed moderate growth of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and he was treated with a seven-day course of IV piperacillin-tazobactam. He developed mild antibiotic-associated diarrhea, managed with loperamide, and transient elevations in creatinine and liver enzymes, which resolved by discharge. Wound care and dermatology optimized his dressing regimen, including acetic acid soaks and alternating topical metronidazole and gentamicin. His pain improved, infection markers normalized, and he was discharged home on oral azithromycin with continued home medications, including IL-2 as part of a clinical trial, and close outpatient follow-up.

ointment applied to ulcers with minimal use of moisturizing

amoxicillin 500 TID and cipro 750 BID per ID recs with f/u in

days prior to his admission. He stated that he gets diarrhea 
when his GVHD and infection flare. We tested a C-diff given 
recent history of abx and it was negative. Treated with imodium 
for one day then resolved.

stated he gets sometimes with GVHD flare (seems to have 
involvement of all mucosal linings). UA was negative and the 
dysuria resolved within a couple days of admission.
